ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the picture, there is a tablecloth whose outer outline is a square. The black area forms a border, and there is a white square in the middle. On the border there are several congruent light-colored small squares, all rotated into a diamond orientation, and the diagonals of these small squares are parallel to the sides of the tablecloth. Along the top side, 5 light-colored small diamonds can be counted, and along the bottom side there are also 5; on the left and right sides there are 3 light-colored small diamonds each that do not overlap with the top and bottom sides, so there are a total of 16 light-colored small squares. Reasoning: Let the diagonal length of each light-colored small square be d. From the arrangement of the diagonals of the 5 small squares on the top side, it can be known that the side length of the entire outer square tablecloth is 5d, so the total area is (5d)^2 = 25d^2. The middle white square is at a distance of one small square diagonal length d from each outer side, so the side length of the middle white square is 5d - 2d = 3d, and its area is (3d)^2 = 9d^2. The area of each light-colored small square equals d^2/2, so the total area of the 16 light-colored small squares is 16·d^2/2 = 8d^2. Black area = total area - middle white area - total area of the light-colored small squares = 25d^2 - 9d^2 - 8d^2 = 8d^2. Therefore, the proportion of the black part to the whole tablecloth is 8d^2 / 25d^2 = 8/25 = 32%.

The 5 top diamonds show that the outer square side is 5 small-square diagonals long. The central white square begins one such diagonal in from each side, so its side is 3 small-square diagonals. Let one small light square have diagonal d. Then the whole tablecloth area is (5d)^2 = 25d^2. The central white square area is (3d)^2 = 9d^2.
